chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said to Ghālib ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah, the father of al-Farazdaq, during a conversation between them:
What about the large number of your camels?

key_terms.أَبِى الْفَرَزْدَقِ: Father of al-Farazdaq, the famous Arabic poet
key_terms.إِبِلُكَ: Your camels (plural of camel, indicating wealth/livestock)
key_terms.غَالِبِ بْنِ صَعْصَعَةَ: Ghālib ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah, a companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ask Ghālib ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah about his camels?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) inquires about the wealth of Ghālib ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah, the father of the renowned poet al-Farazdaq, using the metaphor of 'camels' to discuss material prosperity. This interaction, recorded in *Nahj al-Balagha*, reflects the socio-economic context of the early Islamic community and serves as a prelude to discussing how such wealth was utilized in fulfilling religious and social obligations.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 446. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said to Ghālib ibn Ṣa‘ṣa‘ah, the father of al-Farazdaq (the famous Arabic poet) during a conversation between them:
What about the large number of your camels?
